questions.solution:

Let initial Income = 100, Spending = 80, Savings = 20.

Income ↑ 20% → 120.

Spending ↑ 10% → 80 + 8 = 88.

New Savings = 120 − 88 = 32.

Savings % increase = ((32 − 20) ÷ 20) × 100 = 60%.

60% in decimal = 0.6.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

Spending = 80% of Income

Income increase = 20%

Spending increase = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage change = (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value × 100

 Initial State (Income = 100)
 
 Spend: 80
 
 Save: 20
 New State (Income = 120)
 
 Spend: 88 (+10%)
 
 Save: 32
 
• 
 Savings Increase: 20 → 32 (60%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original Income = 100 units

⇒ Original Expenditure = 80% of 100 = 80 units

⇒ Original Savings = 100 − 80 = 20 units

⇒ New Income = 100 × (1 + 20/100) = 120 units

⇒ New Expenditure = 80 × (1 + 10/100) = 80 + 8 = 88 units

⇒ New Savings = 120 − 88 = 32 units

⇒ Increase in Savings = 32 − 20 = 12 units

⇒ Percentage Increase = (12 ÷ 20) × 100 = 60%

⇒ Value in decimal = 60 ÷ 100 = 0.6

**∴ The correct option is C.**

Percentage Change Relation

Net Income Change % = (Exp % × Exp Change %) + (Sav % × Sav Change %). In this case: 20 = (0.8 × 10) + (0.2 × x), solving for x gives 60%.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a monopoly?

options.text: Full control over the price by the seller

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One buyer and many sellers**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A monopoly is characterized by **one seller and many buyers**.
 
• In a monopoly, there are **no close substitutes** for the product or service provided by the seller.
 
• The seller in a monopoly has **full control over the price** of the product or service.
 
• The market condition of **one buyer and many sellers** describes a monopsony, not a monopoly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **monopoly** exists when a specific person or enterprise is the only supplier of a particular commodity.
 
• This contrasts with a **monopsony** where there is only one buyer and many sellers.
 
• Monopolies can be established by a government, form naturally over time, or form as a conglomerate of companies.
 
• Monopolies can lead to **higher prices and inferior products** due to the lack of competition.
 
• Antitrust laws in many countries regulate monopolistic practices to protect consumers.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sat Nov 26 1949 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.
 
• While the Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949, it **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **97 topics** are currently listed in India's Union List.
 
• The Union List is one of the **three lists** in the **Seventh Schedule** to the Constitution of India, granting powers to the Union government to legislate on these topics.
 
• Subjects under the **Union List include defense, foreign affairs, railways, banking, among others,** where the central government has exclusive powers to legislate.
 
• The list reflects the subjects that are of national importance and require uniformity of legislation across the country.
